title: Staggered activation patterns and ops hackpad (wip)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a working hackpad for staggered activation (aka "staged traffic activation") patterns we want to standardize across the Console + Router + Serving teams. It sits between the high-level rollout playbooks and the operational runbooks — mostly an engineering-first capture of patterns, failure modes, and lightweight coordination rituals for cross-functional rollouts (canary, A/B, progressive exposures).

Why another doc?
- Many canary/playbooks exist, but we still see ad-hoc traffic slices and inconsistent gating signals.
- This tries to codify a small set of pragmatic activation patterns, safety primitives, and a minimal ceremony for low-friction experiments and feature launches.

Key design goals (tradeoffs):
- Fast iteration: low ceremony for low-risk changes (UI flags, non-customer-impacting defaults).
- Safety-first for model/serving changes: strict metric guardrails and automated eviction paths.
- Cross-team clarity: explicit ownerships + signal owners for each rollout.
- Reproducible rollback: one-button revert for routing + quick model fallback.

Novel primitives in this hackpad (sketches):
- Traffic Escrow: hold traffic in a logically isolated queue while we validate downstream instrumentation (synthetic probes, tracing). Only release R% after an explicit commit event or passing instrumentation health checks. Useful when enabling new observability or complex routing rules.
- Metric Lease: short-term exclusive ownership of a metric stream by the experiment owner for the first 10-30 minutes to prevent noisy global dashboards from triggering false alarms. After lease TTL, metric ownership falls back to normal dashboards.
- Canary Tenure: a mandatory minimum observation window per canary phase defined by tokens and time (e.g., min 12,000 tokens or 30 minutes) to reduce small-sample flukes.

Activation patterns (concrete):
1) Incremental percent ramp (classic): 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%
   - Use when routing decision is stable and cost delta is moderate.
   - Guardrail checks at each step (see below).

2) Step-and-hold with escrow commit:
   - Setup: create escrow queue for new variant, warm caches with synthetic requests, verify traces.
   - Hold at 0% until escrow health checks pass, then commit release to 2% live traffic.
   - Useful for model weight swaps that require cache warm-up.

3) Orthogonal split (A/B orthogonally across cohorts):
   - Partition by cohort attribute (region, plan, user-agent) rather than random percentage.
   - Use to control for environmental confounds (e.g., GPU region differences).

4) Canary with immediate fallback:
   - Route new variant only for traffic that has a fallback route configured. If new variant returns an error or slow response (p95 > threshold), automatically fall back to the baseline model inline.

Essential metrics and definitions (owner + alert thresholds):
- Latency p50 / p95 / p99 (ms) — owner: infra-observability
  - Alert if p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.5 for 5m sustained or p99 spikes > baseline_p99 * 2.
- Success rate (200 OK / total) — owner: serving-runtime
  - Alert if success_rate drops by absolute 0.5% for > 5m at canary-sized traffic or > 0.2% at >25% traffic.
- Error type ratio (timeout vs 5xx vs model-exception) — owner: serving-runtime
  - If timeout proportion > 30% of errors, prefer capacity/latency rollback. If 5xx dominates, prefer config/model rollback.
- Quality signal: regression_in_prompt_suite (A/B BLEU-like or eval-set pass rate) — owner: applied-ml/product
  - Must run deterministic quality checks on a standard prompt set. Block ramp if quality delta > configurable threshold (suggest 1.5% absolute for core prompts).
- Safety events / safety classifier rate — owner: safety-team
  - Any increase in classified safety hits must be manually reviewed; auto-block if severe.

Pre-rollout checklist (mandatory for model/serving changes):
- [ ] Ticket in Jira with rollout plan + gate owners (ENG-XXXX).
- [ ] Small synthetic load tests show stable latency and success at target QPS.
- [ ] Observability hooks: tracing, per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdown live.
- [ ] Run quality eval on baseline + candidate (same prompt seeds) and attach report.
- [ ] Safety review sign-off (safety-team).
- [ ] Slack announce in #prod-rollouts 1 hour before start with commit window.

Phase ceremony (owner responsibilities):
- Phase owner (usually release engineer or PM): executes route ramp and clicks commit.
- Signal owners: infra, serving-runtime, applied-ml. Each has 1st-response on-call for the canary window.
- Communications owner: posts updates in Slack and triggers a post-mortem if rollback occurs.

Automated rollback criteria (examples to implement):
- If p95 latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes -> auto-rollback.
- If success_rate delta < -0.5% sustained 5 minutes -> auto-rollback.
- If quality regression on core prompt set > threshold on hourly re-eval -> notify and pause ramp.

Low-friction A/B experiments (product features):
- Use feature flags + variant tagging (not models) for UI/behavior experiments.
- Expose a lightweight A/B template that wires up metrics, sample size calculator, and recommended exposure schedule.
- Default experiment length: 7 days, but for high-variance signals require larger samples (sample calculator link).

Observability playbook (what we look at in the first 30 minutes):
- Synthetic probe latency and success rate (global).
- Real traffic p50/p95 and small-sample noise plots (token count annotated).
- Error breakdown and top-10 failing request IDs for root-cause.
- Quality eval snapshot vs baseline on canonical prompt set.
- Cost-rate change (tokens/sec and estimated $/hour) — show if new variant is 2x cost.

Post-rollout: immediate housekeeping
- Save experiment snapshot (routes, model versions, metric baselines) for 30 days.
- Create a short post-rollout note: success/failure, anomalies, follow-ups. Attach to Jira ticket.
- If rollout lasted > 24 hours, schedule 1-hour async review across owners to capture lessons learned.

Known failure modes (from recent incidents):
- Small-sample variance triggered premature rollback: mitigation -> Canary Tenure + Metric Lease.
- Cache cold-start causing p95 spikes: mitigation -> Traffic Escrow + synthetic warms.
- Region-specific infra throttles: mitigation -> orthogonal splits, guardrails per-region.

Open questions / TODOs:
- SLA for Metric Lease TTL — default 10 minutes? Who enforces? (ask infra observability).
- How to surface escrow status in Console UI succinctly. (PM + frontend).
- Should we require signing a "commit window" for any >10% exposure? (ops policy).
- Integrate a small-sample statistical test (Bayesian A/B) into Console before allowing ramp.

Quick references and templates (placeholders):
- Slack post template: "Start canary: {change}, route:{route}, phases: 0->1->5->25, ticket: ENG-XXXX, watchers: @infra @serving @ml"
- Jira rollout template: short checklist + metric owners.
- Minimal guardrail config JSON (example) -> put in ENG-6128 PR.

Notes to self (choppy):
- push ML eval hooks to CI so we can run small evals during canary automatically.
- think about a "safety stunt double" route (run safety classifier in parallel on all traffic but don't block; compare rates).
- document cost-exposure calc per experiment (tokens * price profile).

If you're reading this and have a concrete example where the above would have prevented a rollback, paste the incident timeline here and we can iterate.

-- end of hackpad --

(For finalization, move contents into the canonical rollout playbook and create a short deck describing Traffic Escrow and Metric Lease. Assign ENG-6205 for implementation tasks.)
